question: Which function replaces matlab.addons.install?
answer:
Based on MATLAB R2026b [3].

`mpminstall` replaces `matlab.addons.install`, which is marked "not recommended" since R2026b [3]. There are no plans to remove `matlab.addons.install`, but `mpminstall` offers more flexible options for installing and managing add-ons [3]. In the same change, `mpmuninstall` and `mpmlist` replace the other `matlab.addons` management functions [2].

The documented update patterns are:

```matlab
% Not recommended
installedAddon = matlab.addons.install("C:\Downloads\My toolbox.mltbx")
installedAddon = matlab.addons.install("C:\Downloads\My toolbox.mltbx","overwrite")
installedAddon = matlab.addons.install("C:\Downloads\My toolbox.mltbx","add")

% Recommended
installedAddon = mpminstall("C:\Downloads\My toolbox.mltbx")
installedAddon = mpminstall("C:\Downloads\My toolbox.mltbx",AllowVersionReplacement=true)
installedAddon = mpminstall("C:\Downloads\My toolbox.mltbx",AllowVersionReplacement=false)
```

These map to the three calls in the "Not Recommended" and "Recommended" table of the `matlab.addons.install` page, in order [3]. The `agreeToLicense` argument is no longer supported, and license agreement approval now happens by default [3].

studyNotes.focus: The question asks which function replaces the (now not recommended) matlab.addons.install for installing add-ons in MATLAB.

keyPoints.text: matlab.addons.install is not recommended as of R2026b; mpminstall is the recommended replacement for installing add-ons.
The R2026b migration table maps matlab.addons.install(fileName) to mpminstall(fileName), and the overwrite option to mpminstall with AllowVersionReplacement=true.
The matlab.addons functions are not removed, but mpminstall, mpmuninstall and mpmlist are recommended for managing add-ons, including enabling or disabling them.
The matlab.addons.install agreeToLicense argument is no longer supported in R2026b because license agreement approval now occurs by default.

mayBeStale.text: R2026b is the current release as of the 2026-11-13 date, and these migration details come from R2026b documentation which may change in later releases.
The source page for matlab.addons.install notes that it only supports toolbox installation and that add-on management functions may change in a future release.
